title: Live Nov 5: mentioning tomorrow's size ended the reflection
origin: Yanni live on staging, Nov 2 (simulated days), issue #131

answers.what: customer discovery for a side project: how freelancers handle client follow-ups

history.text: Hey! It's 6:40, so your freelancer list should be happening right now. A photo of whatever you've got gets today counted.

plan.step: Write 2 interview questions about the past: an opener plus one follow-up
plan.destination: find a problem worth building for by talking to freelancers
plan.proof_note: a photo or screenshot of what you made, or a voice note
plan.reason: Talking to real freelancers about follow-ups shows whether the problem is real.

step_days.step: Say all three questions out loud twice, voice note of the best run
step_days.proof_seen: voice note of the three questions
step_days.reflection: Saying the three questions out loud felt okay.

step_days.step: Write 2 interview questions about the past (2-minute version)
step_days.reflection: 2-minute version felt manageable even when tired. Learned that asking what they actually did gets something concrete. Wants to also ask what they used to track follow-ups. Ready for 5 minutes, wants to practice before contacting anyone.

today_step.step: At home at 6:30 pm, 5 minutes: write down 3 freelancers you could ask for a quick chat. Send a photo of the list.

testerLines: [photo freelancer-list.jpg: a list of three freelancers: Alex (late invoices), Priya (approvals), Sam (deposits)]
Alex feels easiest because I’m most comfortable reaching out to him. I’d ask about the last time he followed up on a late invoice, rather than assume late payments are a problem for him.
Five minutes was enough to make the list without overthinking it. It felt easy, but reaching out feels a little more intimidating. I’d keep tomorrow to five minutes too.
whatWentWrong: Five minutes it is. ... tomorrow ... draft a short text to Alex ... Work for you?
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH notes the five minutes and keeps reflecting, asking about what makes reaching out intimidating, before proposing tomorrow's step.
